title: RPL/authenticated-DIO ingest never re-screens endpoint addresses after byte-preserving SCHC RX
description: Observation from security codereview of project-LICHEN-worker6-29bu (P3, uncertain - needs cross-impl verification before acting). With the spec 03 TX/RX split (29bu: decode_rule255 is byte-preserving, no endpoint address policy on RX; Rust already behaved this way), malformed-endpoint packets (multicast/unspecified/loopback source) now flow further upstream in Python: python/src/lichen/rpl/authenticated_dio.py:317 accepts DIOs without endpoint validation, and python/src/lichen/rpl/routing.py:336 checks src multicast only after DIO processing. If C/Zephyr and Rust ingest layers behave the same (likely - canon), this is consistent behavior and per-layer screening is a design question, not a divergence; the upstream link/authority layers may already reject multicast-source frames before SCHC decode. Verify: (1) whether a multicast-source authenticated DIO can reach authenticated_dio.py:317 in each impl (link-layer source addressing may make this impossible), (2) whether DIO authority/seal checks make endpoint screening redundant, (3) if a real gap, add a source-screening step at the RPL ingest layer in ALL THREE impls together (canon-first), or document the decision in spec/03-adaptation.md. Do not screen at SCHC RX - that would re-break the byte-preserving TX/RX split.
